issues.description: The problem statement contains an internal contradiction about the type of the Farm.animals collection: the UML in the problem shows animals: List<Animal> (implying a List), while the textual instructions require using a Set implemented as a HashSet to ensure unique animals. The provided solution implements animals as a List/ArrayList, and the template leaves the collection unimplemented. This mismatch (UML vs. textual requirement vs. solution) will confuse students about which collection type to use and may cause tests expecting uniqueness (Set behavior) to fail if students follow the solution or UML instead of the textual requirement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intended collection type consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement UML to show animals: Set<Animal> (and clarify use of HashSet), and update the solution/template to declare private Set<Animal> animals and initialize it as new HashSet<>() with corresponding getter/setter and addAnimal using set.add(...); or (B) If List is intended, update the textual instructions to remove the HashSet/Set requirement and ensure UML and solution use List consistently. Prefer option A if uniqueness is pedagogically required.

issues.description: The conceptual entity 'the collection of animals in Farm' is referenced with different collection types across artifacts: the UML in the problem statement shows a List<Animal> attribute, the textual requirements explicitly require a Set implemented as a HashSet (to enforce uniqueness), and the solution implements a List/ArrayList. This mismatch obscures the intended requirement (unique animals without duplicates) and forces students to reconcile conflicting instructions about which collection type to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the specification and implementation to use the same collection type. Prefer the textual requirement (Set/HashSet) which enforces uniqueness: update the UML and any references to List to specify Set<Animal>, and modify the solution (and template) to declare 'private Set<Animal> animals' initialized as 'new HashSet<>()', adjusting getters/setters and usage accordingly. Alternatively, if List is intended, change the textual requirement to remove the 'Set/HashSet' mandate so all artifacts consistently reference List/ArrayList.
